data.name: Dhruv
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Dhruv is the name of a king who was cursed to become a stone. He was later rewarded with a place in the sky as the North Star, Polaris, which is a symbol of unwavering devotion and steadfastness.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dhruv is often used as a honorific or spiritual name in India, signifying unwavering devotion, determination, and resilience. It also has roots in traditional Indian dance and music, with several compositions dedicated to Lord Dhruva, the star.
data.spiritual_significance: The legend of Dhruv teaches about the importance of unwavering devotion and faith in God. Despite being cursed to become a stone, Dhruv continued to pray and remained steadfast in his devotion. His story serves as an inspiration for self-discipline, determination, and the power of faith in achieving spiritual goals.

historical_references.reference: Legend has it that King Bharata, the father of Lord Rama, had a charioteer named Dhruva. Dhruva was an ungrateful and disrespectful boy who doubted his father's superiority and even challenged him to a chariot race. In anger, King Bharata expelled Dhruva from the kingdom. Dhruva, repentant and seeking forgiveness, went to the sage Trisanku for guidance. Trisanku, who was a great devotee of Lord Vishnu, advised Dhruva to meditate on Vishnu and offered him a place in the heavens as a reward for his devotion.

Dhruv was also a celebrated astronomer and mathematician. He is credited with being the first to calculate the position of the North Star, which is called Polaris or Dhruva Tara in Indian astronomy. According to the Mahabharata, Dhruva was the son of King Uttanapada and Renuka. When Dhruva was a young prince, he doubted his father's supremacy and was cursed by the sage Vashisttha to be born as a star in the constellation of Ursa Minor. After many hardships and penance, he was released from his curse and attained a place in the heavens as the North Star.
